title: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction
claim: A two-stage method turns sparse observations into a full field by fitting a physics-constrained spatial decoder, then modeling a continuous trajectory.
layout: Left-to-right: input volume, central framework box with two modules, output volume; PDE loss on top
description: The figure runs left to right. On the left, a stack of sparse, irregularly masked ocean-field frames (red/blue with black gaps) sits under a time arrow T and is labeled 'Sparse irregular observations'. A large rounded box titled 'PhysFTM' fills the middle. Its lower left holds 'Functional Tucker modeling': a pink Tucker core cube with three factor functions f¹, f², f³ along modes i1, i2, i3, plus an RKHS surface icon. Its lower right holds 'Continuous trajectory construction': a time axis (t1, t', t_l+1) with 3D coordinate cubes, curved arrows linking blue core cubes, and labels for support-core inference and continuous-time modeling. At the top, a blue box lists the PDE residual and reconstruction error, and a pink box shows differentiation with finite-difference physical loss. Green arrows link these boxes to the modules. On the right, a dense reconstructed field is labeled 'Reconstructed spatiotemporal field'. The eye goes first to the red and blue field images at both ends.
caption: Overall framework of PhysFTM. PhysFTM reconstructs sparse grid-based sensor observations by learning an RKHS-regularized Functional Tucker spatial decoder constrained by observation loss and finite-difference PDE residuals. The inferred Tucker cores are then modeled as a continuous trajectory in core space and decoded back to the physical domain to obtain the reconstructed spatiotemporal field.
abstract: Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. To this end, we propose PhysFTM---a physics-informed functional Tucker model that parameterizes the Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) and incorporates PDE constraints through finite-difference residuals evaluated at off-sensor collocation points. These residuals provide additional physical information in regions without direct observational supervision. PhysFTM first reconstructs continuous spatial fields at support frames via an alternating minimization scheme, optimizing the Tucker core tensor and the RKHS-based factors separately. To enable missing-frame reconstruction, PhysFTM constructs a continuous trajectory in Tucker-core space, which is decoded by the learned spatial RKHS-FTM representation to recover the full spatiotemporal field. Experiments on Allen--Cahn, Navier--Stokes, three-dimensional Heat equations, and a three-dimensional gridded Copernicus ocean reanalysis demonstrate accurate 2D/3D reconstruction under two missing-frame protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/liusirzzz/PhysFTM.
